messages:
acme_app: Hey team — we're seeing partial streaming responses when traffic goes through our gRPC->HTTP1 transcoding gateway. Stream starts, a chunk of tokens arrives, then the connection drops and the client reconnects and often receives duplicate prefix tokens. UX blinks and billing appears to spike. Happening only behind our gateway; direct http2 to Redwood looks fine.

support_maya: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste a minimal repro (curl/httpie) and the gateway type + config? Also confirm whether you're calling the hosted API or Dedicated.

acme_app: Hosted. Repro (simplified) below — run from client behind their gateway and you'll see the partial then reconnect behavior.

acme_app: ```
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate \\n  -d '{"model":"rw-infer-1","input":"stream test\\n","max_tokens":100}'
```

client_log: Example client output when problem occurs:

client_log: data: {"id":"evt-1","text":"Hello wor"}
client_log: <connection reset by peer>
client_log: reconnecting...
client_log: data: {"id":"evt-2","text":"Hello world"}  <-- duplicate prefix + continuation

eng_max: Can you capture a curl -v (request/response headers) or a tcpdump? My suspicion: the gRPC->HTTP1 transcoder or an intermediate proxy is coalescing/chopping chunks incorrectly or timing out and closing the midstream socket, then the client reconnects and the server treats it as a fresh request. That can produce duplicate prefixes. Also need to know if the gateway is doing grpc-web or JSON transcoding.

acme_app: curl -v response headers we see (redacted):

acme_app: ```
> GET /v1/streams/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.ai
> Accept: text/event-stream
> Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< transfer-encoding: chunked
< content-type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
< x-envoy-upstream-service-time: 42
< x-accel-buffering: no
```

eng_max: Thanks — that helps. Two likely failure modes we've seen: (1) the gateway buffers several small server chunks and emits a larger coalesced chunk; if the gateway then hits an internal timeout/health-check/reset it can close the TCP connection leaving the client with a partial prefix; when the client reconnects the server generates the prefix again (new request) causing duplicated tokens. (2) grpc-web/transcoding stacks sometimes rewrite framing and strip trailer metadata, which can trigger intermediate resets.

support_maya: Quick troubleshooting steps to try on your side:
- Bypass the gateway and call Redwood over plain HTTP/2 (if possible) to confirm behavior disappears.
- Disable buffering/response coalescing on the gateway (envoy/nginx: proxy_buffering off / X-Accel-Buffering: no).
- If using grpc-transcoder/grpc-web, enable passthrough streaming mode or use a dedicated streaming route that does not aggregate bodies.
- Add idempotency on the client: track event ids from the stream so duplicates are ignored.

acme_app: We tried disabling buffering on nginx and set X-Accel-Buffering: no, still occasional duplicates. We noticed the gateway auth service occasionally times out (200ms spikes) and then closes the upstream connection — that's tightly correlated. When auth times out the proxy tears down the stream mid-response. Could that be the real trigger?

eng_max: Yes — an upstream async auth or ext-auth filter that delays can cause the proxy to close or restart the stream mid-flight. When that happens the server (Redwood) has already emitted tokens; on reconnect it's a new request and we re-emit. That explains the billing spike (two separate requests = two billing events).

support-billing-bot: Note: reconnects that result in separate HTTP requests are treated as separate streaming sessions for billing. We can investigate and, if there's evidence of repeated replays due to a gateway bug, make an adjustment. Please open a billing support ticket with: request id + first/second request timestamps + customer account id.

eng_max: For us: next internal steps — (A) can you share a pcap or nginx/envoy config snippets for the streaming route and any ext-auth timeouts? (B) we'll pull server-side traces for the request ids you provided to confirm duplicate token emission and attach logs for billing.

acme_app: Sharing config & pcap now (uploaded). Our env has ext_authz with a 300ms timeout and the route uses grpc_json_transcoder.

eng_max: Follow-up notes / mitigation:
- Short term: route streaming requests directly to a passthrough upstream (http2) or bump ext_authz timeout and ensure no per-request buffering.
- Mid term: runtime team will add an optional de-dup window: if a new request for the same stream/session id arrives within N seconds and the previous session ended with an upstream reset, server can attempt safe dedupe for prefix tokens (internal RFC being drafted).
- Client-side: implement de-duping by event id and backoff reconnects instead of immediate reissue.

support_maya: I've opened an internal ticket (infra-1202) to track the runtime dedupe work and billing investigation. Eng will reach out with steps once we have traces. :eyes:

acme_app: Thanks — mitigation plan in progress. We'll roll the passthrough route for streaming endpoints this afternoon and monitor. Appreciate the quick triage. :thumbsup:
